items.title: A Team of Researchers from Columbia and CertiK Introduce TensorLean for Formal Verification of GPU Kernels
items.summary: TensorLean, from Columbia University and CertiK, formally verifies production GPU kernels at the PTX level using Lean. It checked 149 kernel instances, proved 83 correct, and found 38 bugs in FlashAttention, DeepGEMM and more.

items.title: Google AI Previews Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API for Large Tool Libraries
items.summary: Google launched Gemini API Tool Retrieval in preview. Agents keep a large tool library on standby and load each parameter schema only when needed, inside one Interactions API request.

items.summary: Major US financial institutions are banning third-party bots from logging into your accounts—and warning that any costly bot mistakes are strictly your problem.

items.title: Security researchers show how cheap AI inference providers steal keys and snoop on users
items.summary: Security researchers at Dragos used two million fake AI requests to uncover serious vulnerabilities in the AI supply chain, finding at least three compromised providers, hundreds of stolen AWS keys, and marketplace resellers who were simply reading customer requests. OpenRouter responded by removing three providers and 125 endpoints.

items.title: AI is getting better faster than experts can reliably test whether new systems are safe, METR warns
items.summary: METR reports that leading AI models like Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra are improving rapidly at research tasks but getting harder to measure. Current data can't rule out a dangerous acceleration in AI development, the organization warns, though it also says common tests may overestimate what the models can actually do.

items.title: Perplexity's new Monitor API turns web search from a one-off query into a nonstop watchdog
items.summary: Perplexity is launching a Monitor API that searches the web on a schedule and alerts agents via webhook only when relevant changes occur. Its own decision model filters out unimportant results.

items.title: AI coding agents ace isolated tests but complete fewer than one in ten tasks in a simulated workplace
items.summary: A new real-world test puts AI coding agents in a simulated developer job with colleagues, project boards, and incomplete handoffs, where they have to keep developing software on their own and reliably close open tickets in a messy daily workflow. Even Opus 5.5 and Astra fall far short, solving fewer than one in ten tasks completely.

items.title: Binding of Isaac developer removes AI music from Repentance Plus
items.summary: The Binding of Isaac: Repentance Plus has spent the last few days getting review-bombed on Steam after it was discovered that a particular segment of the game used AI music. Reddit user ShweetsStuff discovered the songs used during a Grand Theft Auto-themed section.

items.summary: AI now sits on both sides of the security fight, and the vocabulary has changed with it. IBM’s 2026 Cost of a Data Breach Report found that 1 in 4 malicious breaches were AI-enabled, up 56% year over year.

items.title: Z.ai follows OpenAI into loop transformer territory with its new 750B flagship model
items.summary: Z.ai is moving its flagship GLM-5.4 model to a loop architecture in which 28 layers run twice, which the company says lets the 750-billion-parameter model match models with 2 to 3 trillion parameters. Benchmark scores are only available for a smaller 30B test model so far, and Z.ai is positioning GLM-5.4 as the start of "Generalized Coding," where code also generates videos, games, and CAD models.
